description.narrative: Huvudsyftet med OHCHR 2025-2026 regionala program för mänskliga rättigheter är att stärka kapaciteten hos regionala aktörer och nationella institutioner att främja och skydda mänskliga rättigheter inom migration, rättsstatsprincipen, miljö och klimatförändringar, medborgerligt utrymme samt hållbart företagande.

The main objective of the OHCHR 2025-2026 regional human rights programme is to strengthen the capacity of regional actors and national institutions to promote and protect human rights in the areas of migration, the rule of law, environment and climate change, civic space, and sustainable business.

The main objective of the OHCHR 2025-2026 regional human rights programme is to strengthen the capacity of regional actors and national institutions to promote and protect human rights in the areas of migration, the rule of law, environment and climate change, civic space, and sustainable business.
The programme is an integral part of OHCHRs regional strategy and priorities and is aligned with OHCHRs global goals and work to strengthen the thematic capacities of regional offices. The programme strengthens existing structures and enables OHCHR to intensify its work in the six result areas: 1. Laws, policies and practices on governance in the administration of justice and in law enforcement address and prevent human rights violations and abuses. 2. CSOs, victims, witnesses, and their families, at regional and national levels, are increasingly able to effectively access and engage with formal and informal justice mechanisms, including on violations linked to business activities and environmental rights. 3. The right to a clean, healthy, and sustainable environment increasingly guides economic activities and environmental actions 4. State institutions enhance their engagement with international human rights mechanisms, increase reporting to them and improve implementation of their outcomes. 5. States adopt laws, policies, programmes and practices to combat all forms of discrimination and address inequalities including their intersectional dimensions, informed by disaggregated data. 6. Legal, regulatory, institutional and policy frameworks protect and expand civic space offline and online.
